about.title: Dunsmuir Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Dunsmuir sits along I-5 in Siskiyou County, a small town of roughly 1,582 people where daily life often involves the same tools, vehicles, and household products found everywhere else in California. When one of those products fails — a car part gives out on I-5, a tool breaks on the job, or an appliance malfunctions at home — the injury can be sudden and serious. California law generally allows an injured person to pursue a defective-product claim under strict liability, meaning the focus is on whether the product itself was flawed, not on proving carelessness by the manufacturer. That can apply to design flaws, manufacturing defects, or inadequate warnings. We handle product liability cases throughout Siskiyou County and beyond, and we can help you understand whether you have a claim. Our team reviews what happened and identifies who may be responsible — the maker, distributor, or retailer.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to Us About a Product Defect

items.title: You Don't Have to Prove Negligence
items.desc: Under California's strict liability rules, the question is usually whether the product was defective, not whether the manufacturer was careless. We can help identify which type of defect applies to your situation.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable for a defective product. Our team can sort out which parties were involved in getting that product to you.

items.title: Keeping the Product Matters
items.desc: California product cases often depend heavily on examining the item itself. We can advise you on preserving evidence before it's lost, altered, or discarded.

items.question: What counts as a defective product under California law?
items.answer: Generally, a product can be considered defective if it has a design flaw, a manufacturing error, or inadequate warnings and instructions. California's strict liability standard means you typically don't need to prove the company was negligent — just that the defect existed and caused your injury. We can help evaluate which category fits your case.

items.question: I live in a small town like Dunsmuir — can I still find help with a product liability claim?
items.answer: Yes. Dunsmuir's size doesn't limit your legal options; we handle product liability cases throughout Siskiyou County and beyond. Contact us for a free case review, no matter how small or remote your community is.

items.question: Should I keep the product that hurt me?
items.answer: In most cases, yes — preserving the actual product is often important evidence in a strict liability claim. Try not to repair, modify, or discard it, and store it somewhere safe until you've spoken with us about next steps.
